#817. Avril Lavigne Welcomes First Baby

Avril Lavigne shared she has welcomed her first child, giving a glimpse at her and her unnamed partner's baby girl: “Our mini f--king princess has arrived.”

The "Sk8er Boi" musician recently shared a major glimpse into her private world, confirming she is now a mom after welcoming her first child, a baby girl.

"Our mini f--king princess," she captioned a Nov. 13 Instagram post featuring photos of her holding her daughter, three pairs of vans as well as her hand and another holding their baby's finger, "has arrived.”

Prior to expanding her family, over the years, Lavigne, 42—who hasn't shared details about the identity of her baby's father—has kept her personal life close to the vest.

She was married to Sum 41 alum Deryck Whibley for three years until 2009, ending their relationship on amicable terms.

"Deryck and I have been together for 6-and-a-half years,” she wrote on her website at the time. “We have been friends since I was 17, started dating when I was 19, and married when I was 21. I am grateful for our time together, and I am grateful and blessed for our remaining friendship."

In fact, their breakup just wasn’t complicated.

"I admire Deryck and have a great amount of respect for him,” she continued. “He is the most amazing person I know and I love him with all my heart. Deryck and I are separating and moving forward on a positive note.”

And when she met second husband Chad Kroeger in 2012, she ultimately decided that she wanted to be more than just his girlfriend, with the couple exchanging vows just a year later. However, by 2015, her relationship with the Nickelback singer met a different ending.

"It is with [a] heavy heart that Chad and I announce our separation today,” she wrote on social media at the time. “Through not only the marriage, but the music as well, we've created many unforgettable moments. We are still, and forever will be, the best of friends, and will always care deeply for each other. To all our family, friends and fans, thank you sincerely for the support."

Since then, Lavigne has been linked to Brody Jenner, Mod Sun and most recently in 2023, Tyga. And though she’s rarely shared insight into her personal life, the “Complicated” singer has opened up about taking a step back from the spotlight entirely.

"I spent the last few years at home sick fighting Lyme Disease,” she wrote on her personal website in 2018. “Those were the worst years of my life as I went through both physical and emotional battles. I was able to turn that fight into music I'm really proud of. I wrote songs in my bed and on the couch and recorded there mostly as well. Words and lyrics that were so true to my experience came pouring out of me effortlessly. Truly... by keeping my spirits up, having goals to reach and a purpose to live for, my music helped to heal me and keep me alive."

"I'm taking my life back into my own hands and doing what it is I know I am meant to be doing in this life time,” she added. “Making music.”

For a look at all the celebs who have had babies rock their worlds this year, keep reading...

The Big Bang Theory alum gave birth to her second baby, a girl named Philomena Carmine Bobby Pelphrey, with the Task actor on Oct. 12.

"There are no words to describe this feeling once again. What a blessing," Cuoco—who's also mom to daughter Matilda—shared on instagram. "We are so grateful for the crazy wild up and down journey that brought us to our little Philo! Family officially complete."

The Indianapolis Colts cornerback and his fiancée Monique Cook shared that they welcomed their third baby, a boy named Chosen Mani Ward, on Sept. 28.

The two are already parents to son Charvarius Ward Jr. as well as daughter Amani Joy, who died in 2024 at 23 months.

The Grey's Anatomy alum confirmed the arrival of his baby with the Spanish actress in a hilarious video recreating Spike Lee's 1989 movie Do The Right Thing.

Life got sweeter for the Disney Channel alum and the Victoria's Secret model after she gave birth to their first child—a baby girl—in early September.

Hinting at their daughter's birth date, the couple wrote on Instagram, "We took Labor Day literally this year."

Hold on tight, spider monkey—because the Twilight alum and his wife welcomed their first baby together on Sept. 16.

And yes, the couple did make a reference to their identical names when choosing a moniker for their new daughter Lennon Taylor Lautner.

Over one year after adopting their daughter, the Stranger Things star and the Sweethearts actor added a baby boy to their family, writing on Instagram in September 2026, "hi little guy!"

The Girls actress shared on Sept. 16 that the pair welcomed their first child, a daughter, via surrogate.

“Hello. I’m your mama," she recalled telling her baby in a Vogue essay. "You … you look nothing like I thought you would, but exactly right. We’ve been waiting for you, do you know that? It was so nice of you to come.”

On Sept. 11, multiple outlets reported that the "Born This Way" singer and her fiancé of over two years had welcomed their first baby together.

A birth certificate obtained by E! News later revealed that their child—a girl named Rose Bean Polansky—was born on June 9 in Los Angeles.

You can count on the Duggars to expand their brood. The 19 Kids & Counting alum and his wife announced the arrival of their fourth baby on Aug. 7, writing on Instagram, "Life feels busier than ever, yet we find ourselves trying to slow down to just soak in these days with our littles. And we wouldn’t have it any other way!"

John Lennon and Yoko Ono's son announced that he and his partner welcomed a baby boy in a Sept. 1 social media post.

"Okay so…Charlotte and I would like to announce that [we] have indeed created a Human Bean!"  Ono Lennon wrote. "His name is, Aurelius! Thank you!"

The Real Housewives of New Jersey alum Caroline Manzo's son welcomed his second child with his wife, who captioned photos of their newborn baby boy on Aug. 4, "Welcome to the world our sweet Theodore."

The youngest daughter of Prince Andrew and Sarah Ferguson gave birth to her third child—a baby girl—on Aug. 3 at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal.

"The baby was born weighing 6 pounds 9 ounces,"  a statement read on the royal family’s official Instagram page, adding that King Charles III and Queen Camilla "were delighted to be informed of the news.”

The Challenge alums announced that they had welcomed their fifth baby together Aug. 2, less than a year after having their daughter Francesca.

"With a 2-week early grand entrance, we'd like to welcome Vincent John into the world," Compono wrote on Instagram Aug. 3. "What originally was a checkup due to cramping led to a medically necessary induction due to low fluid (Oligo). Love you to bunches, my little Vinny boy."

The Marvel star and the Peaky Blinders actress welcomed their first baby together in July 2026, mulitple outlets reported.

The "I Need to Know" singer became a dad of eight when his wife gave birth to their daughter Myla, sharing in a July 21 that their family is "over the moon."

“What a great blessing to be able to share with you the arrival of our precious MYLA,” the couple wrote in a joint statement. “You can't imagine the happiness we have at home."

On an episode of her LadyGang podcast, the Glee alum announced that her seond baby—a daughter named Meyer June Martin—"decided to make an early entrance into the world."

"She was supposed to be born August 26, and she was born July 19," Tobin revealed, explaining how her surrogate had to induce labor due to preeclampsia. "The doctor was like, 'You know what? At this point, the baby is cooked pretty nicely.'"

This is...a family of five. After announcing their pregnancy in January, the couple confirmed the arrival of their baby boy in July.

"These last couple of weeks have been chaos, but in the best possible way," Mariano wrote in an Instagram post. "Welcome back home Rock-Anthony Makoa Ventimiglia. Can’t wait for all of the adventures ahead with our family of 5!"

The couple—who have been dating since at least 2023—confirmed they welcomed a baby together, with the actor jokingly telling E! News at the premiere of The Hawk, "It's nice to be out before I go back to work on my shift."

The couple announced they'd welcomed their baby on July 1 after Campbell's water broke early.

"Feels like heaven on earth,” she captioned a July 1 video of her cradling the newborn. "Baby is here and healthy.”

Zack Goytowski & Bliss Poureetezadi-Goytowski

Love is unique—just ask the parents of baby boy Polaris J ³ ohn Pax Goytowski.

Yes, the Love Is Blind couple gave their son what they described as a "three-dimensional name represented in two-dimensional space" when he was born on June 29.

The reveal of the unconventional moniker—an homage to three J-named family members—comes two years after the birth of their daughter Galileo Terri Rayne Goytowski.

The When Calls the Heart costars confirmed that they welcomed a baby girl in April, 10 months after they secretly wed in June 2025.

"Our daughter has been the greatest gift,” they told People in an interview published June 23, “and we are loving getting to know her better with each passing day."

The Summer House alum and her boyfriend welcomed their first baby together, Aidan Santos Heavey, on June 21, 10 weeks earlier than expected.

"He's heading to summer camp at NICU for the first 2/3 months in this world, but mom and dad can't wait to bring him home hopefully soon," Heavey wrote on Instagram. "Dad was a nervous, terrified, sobbing mess but couldn't ask for a better first Father's Day."

On June 11, the Dancing With the Stars alum announced she had given birth to her third child, a son named Hayes Duff Cusick, with her husband of 10 years.

"Baby boy is here," she captioned Instagram photos of herself holding the newborn in the hospital after her C-section, "and we are so grateful and so in love."

The Days of Our Lives alum and his wife welcomed their second baby together—a boy named Sebastian Antonio Barash—on June 5.

"House is full," Barash—who also shares son Joaquin with Devoto and daughter Harper with ex-wife Kirsten Storms—wrote on Instagram. "Hearts fuller."

A baby has entered the villa! The Love Island UK couple announced on June 4 that they had welcomed their second baby together—a boy.

The Pentatonix member and his husband welcomed a baby girl named Birde James Hoying via surrogate on June 3.

"The process of us having a child took four or five years," Hoying told People in an interview published June 23. "It's been a long time coming and just looking at her, I started crying because it was just such a beautiful thing that I feel really, really lucky."

The "Big Mama" rapper welcomed her first baby, a girl, with the "Bank Account" artist.

"There were tears and anxiety was through the roof," she noted about her pregnancy in an Apple Music interview published May 29. "It's what I wanted but I was just like, 'Wait, this real life, like am I really ready?' But ultimately, obviously had her and I'm glad I made the decision to do it."

The influencer and DJ welcomed baby girl Juliette July Fedyk on June 1, sharing that she was born early at 33 weeks.

"Suddenly the world just got a whole lot brighter," Madeleine posted to Instagram June 2. "06.01.2026 4lbs and 17.2 inches. We love you so much and are so proud to be your parents x."

The Laguna Beach alum and the NASCAR reporter announced the arrival of their first baby, Rhodes August Colletti, on Instagram May 14.

The Originals couple welcomed their first baby together—a son named Arlo Dominic Krueger—on May 3. King is also mom to two daughters with ex-husband Joe King.

#816. Dark matter breakthrough coming? Euclid space telescope unveils its 1st look into the dark universe (video)

On Thursday (Nov. 12), the Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons. The data release lays the foundation for one of the largest-ever 3D maps of the cosmos and many groundbreaking discoveries about the nature of dark energy and dark matter.

The European Space Agency's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has been called the "Dark Universe Detective" because of its capability to investigate the dual mysteries of dark matter, the universe's most mysterious stuff, and dark energy, the force accelerating the expansion of the universe. Collectively, these cosmic elements are sometimes referred to as the dark universe.

The new data release, designated DR1-Foundation, was built from 13 months of observations and is accompanied by a multitude of images, including large sky mosaics. It marks the first major release of mission data since Euclid launched in mid-2023.

"These are far more than beautiful pictures; today marks a scientific milestone in our study of the cosmos," ESA's Director of Science, Carole Mundell said in a statement. "This major Euclid data release represents the largest space-based survey of its kind, laying the foundation of future discovery in a new regime for astronomy and demonstrating the excellence of European technology, science and international collaboration."

The ESA put into raw numbers the sheer number of celestial objects viewed by the Dark Universe Detective and contained in DR1-Foundation. That includes light spectra from 160 million sources, over 900 million galaxies, and 60 million candidates for quasars, regions of space dominated by feeding supermassive black holes.

"This is a change in scale from Euclid's previous releases, which included a few days of observations over around 60 degrees squared of sky," ESA's Euclid project scientist Valeria Pettorino said. "We're now releasing more than a year of data covering a significantly larger area. This unlocks groundbreaking science."

Euclid can see such a vast number of cosmic objects thanks to the fact that its space-based position helps it avoid interference caused by Earth's atmosphere.

This includes clusters of galaxies and even larger superclusters. The study of these objects, some of the largest structures in the cosmos, can reveal how matter came together across the larger network of gas, dust and dark matter called the cosmic web.

"Euclid doesn't just look far back in time  — it does so across huge areas of sky," Euclid Consortium member Barbara Sartoris of JL Lagrange Laboratory, Nice, France, explained. "This gives us an unprecedented view of large samples of ancient galaxy clusters that were previously out of reach. "We will explore these in the coming months to learn how these giants grew, and decipher what they reveal about the dark universe."

Another exciting element of the new Euclid data release is the 15,000 strong gravitational lensing candidates catalogued by the space telescope. Gravitational lensing is an element of the universe first explained in Einstein magnum opus, general relativity, in 1915.

General relativity says that objects with mass cause the very fabric of space to warp, and that gravity arises from this warping. But there is another consequence. When light passes this curvature, its usually straight path is curved. That means when light from a single background source passes an object with great mass, like a galaxy or galaxy cluster, a strong gravitational lens, it can arrive at our telescopes at different times.

As a result of this strong lensing, background sources can be greatly amplified. It is an effect that the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has been using to great effect to study galaxies in the early universe.

Thus, the prospect of mapping 15,000 strong gravitational lenses is monumental, especially in studying the rate at which the universe is expanding and thus the effect of dark energy.

"Strong lensing provides unique insight into the dark universe, allowing us to 'weigh' individual galaxies, including their invisible dark matter, and explore how the universe is expanding," Natalie Lines of the University of Portsmouth, U.K., and member of the Euclid Consortium, said. "Over 10 years ago, we forecast that Euclid would revolutionize the field of strong lens discovery. That day is finally here."

Arguably, the most exciting thing about DR1-Foundation is that Euclid is just getting started. The area of sky covered from spring 2024 to spring 2025 represents just 14% of Euclid's target for its entire six-year survey.

That means whatever scientists discover from this data release could be the tip of the iceberg in terms of how the Dark Universe Detective will change our understanding of the cosmos.

"DR1-Foundation includes raw data, calibrated images, catalogues, and spectra over a huge sky area, with enough statistics touncover even rare objects," Valeria said. "It will be used to map the large-scale structure of the universe in unprecedented detail.

Robert Lea is a science journalist in the U.K. whose articles have been published in Physics World, New Scientist, Astronomy Magazine, All About Space, Newsweek and ZME Science. He also writes about science communication for Elsevier and the European Journal of Physics. Rob holds a bachelor of science degree in physics and astronomy from the U.K.’s Open University. Follow him on Twitter @sciencef1rst.

#815. Rugby League World Cup finals, ATP and WTA tennis, plus WSL – follow with us

Here’s how to follow along with our coverage – the finest writing and up-to-the-minute reports

Old Trafford and Selhurst Park watchers aside, the break from Premier League events – on the pitch at least – heralds a day of lively international activity. Emillia Hawkins arises bright and early with all the Nations League buildup as Wales, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland bound into view later. There may well be follow-up from Scotland’s Friday night date with North Macedonia and anticipation for England’s clash with Spain on Sunday. Plus, a host of EFL and WSL fixtures will keep the updates flowing. Join the conversation at matchday.live@theguardian.com.

Greg Wood saddles up for a cracking ‘Super Saturday’ in the autumn’s best meeting, with the Paddy Power Gold Cup Handicap Chase front and centre and Ben Pauling’s Meetmebythesea hard to ignore. Elsewhere, Old Park Star could make a winning start over fences in the Arkle Challenge Trophy Trial Novice Chase.

Simon Burnton helms the blog as the WSL’s two unbeaten sides go head to head at lunchtime. Andrée Jeglertz’s City hold top spot after drubbing West Ham 5-0 while Chelsea were held by Everton last weekend. With two points separating the pacesetters, this is a crucial match for Chelsea – lose and their title hopes will become worryingly untethered even at this stage of the season. Suzanne Wrack reports.

Morgan Gillory will be back to solving crimes very soon.

#813. Ferguson 'made up' with first win as Glentoran boss

Duncan Ferguson's home debut with Glentoran ended with a late winner from teenage striker Cal Weatherup

At the third time of asking, Duncan Ferguson is finally up and running as Glentoran manager.

After two draws to start his tenure in the Irish Premiership, a home debut for the former Everton striker had late drama under the Friday night lights at the Oval.

Jordan Stewart, dubbed the "wee man" by big Dunc after his first game, celebrated his contract extension by scoring the opening goal and, in a largely uneventful game, it looked like that would be the difference.

However, that all changed when Ben Cushnie equalised for Bangor in the 83rd minute, but there was more drama to follow as Cal Weatherup raced onto a long ball to slot home the winner with three minutes remaining and secure a first win for Ferguson as boss.

"I'm delighted to get my first three points at home, I'm absolutely made up," Ferguson said after the game.

"The boys kept on going until the very end."

Weatherup's late goal gives Ferguson first Glens win

Ferguson's first game in the Irish League was meant to be at home to Ballymena United on 24 October, but Storm Boelo and a waterlogged pitch delayed his highly-anticipated debut in the league.

Stewart scored the equaliser at then-leaders Coleraine in his first outing in the dugout the following week, and the Glens were then held to a goalless draw at Carrick Rangers.

But on Friday, Ferguson finally announced himself to the home support in east Belfast.

Despite a controlled first half and Stewart's opener, Ferguson felt that his side "sat too deep" before Bangor's equaliser, which came through former Glentoran man Cushnie.

But it was teenager Weatherup who was ultimately the difference, with a finish that Ferguson would have been proud of in his playing days as he slotted the ball between the legs of the onrushing Patrick Solis Grogan for his first goal of the campaign.

Ferguson said he was "made up" for the 18-year-old, who replaced Pat Hoban midway through the second half.

"We showed good character. We showed a bit of resilience," added the 54-year-old.

"They put us under pressure in the second half but that will happen. You're not going to dominate a game for the whole game at any level.

"I was delighted the boys showed character and resilience to get back into the game."

Highlights: Late winner gives Ferguson first victory as Glens boss

Given their mixed start to the season, a charge at the Irish Premiership title is going to be a long shot.

But if the Glens are to have any aspirations of a first Gibson Cup since 2009 then it is important for them to keep pace with those above.

Leaders Linfield and nearest challengers Coleraine both were comfortable winners on Friday, while Larne bounced back from their poor recent win to beat Dungannon Swifts.

Glentoran are 14 points off the Blues but have a game in hand, and they face another tricky home test against Cliftonville next Friday to try and build upon the win over the Seasiders.

As he reflected on his start to the league, Ferguson admitted "I think we need to get better overall.

"We're not conceding many goals, but we just have to create more.

"That's the hardest part of the game, but we look solid and that's the main thing.

"I'm happy with the group and the league is very close together, from top to bottom".

With that in mind, especially as he continues his early steps in the league, it's just "one game at a time" for Ferguson, rather than thinking too far ahead.

"We've just got to keep going. I think that is seven or eight games undefeated now," he added.

"We have to keep going and keep winning. We're a big club and the fans want us to keep winning, and I'm glad we got the three points for them today."

#812. Pochettino’s Chelsea maelstrom the best yardstick for what lies ahead at United

Argentinian oversaw high-scoring games in his one Chelsea season and Opta predicts his Manchester United side will move upfield quicker than that team

Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “big beasts” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager.

Pochettino took over Southampton midway through their first season back in the top flight (2012-13) after the club spent seven years in the lower leagues. In his only full campaign, they finished eighth. He led Tottenham to second in 2016-17, third in the seasons either side, and reached the 2019 Champions League final. His presence lifted those clubs.

However, the Argentinian has competed in only one of the past six Premier League campaigns. Winning Ligue 1 and the Coupe de France in an 18-month spell with Paris Saint-Germain tells us little. His most pertinent recent experience for the Manchester United job is the 2023-24 season he spent at Chelsea, a campaign that left more questions than answers.

The club had finished 12th the season before, in the first year of the Todd Boehly/Clearlake Capital era. Pochettino was always likely to take Chelsea higher. And he did. But his influence is harder to judge. Opta predicted Chelsea would finish sixth in 2023-24, a forecast that proved correct. By this measure Pochettino hit par though, as Transfermarkt rated the market value of his squad as the third-highest in the Premier League in October 2023, perhaps he fell short.

The squad value grew thanks to remarkable investment. Chelsea spent more than any other club in Europe’s big five leagues in each of the three transfer windows from the summer of 2022 to the summer of 2023. Working for Boehly will have provided a good primer for the madness of Manchester United, even if the spending won’t be as generous.

Assembling a winning team from a rapidly evolving squad is not easy. Pochettino crafted a side that delivered the fifth-most expected points in 2023-24. Chelsea’s 63.4 was a fair way shy of Arsenal (81.2), Manchester City (79.3) and Liverpool (76.2) but it was a decent first season.

Chelsea conceded 63 league goals, the club’s worst figure in the Premier League era. Yet only twice have they amassed more than the 77 goals they scored. They were a little above their expected goal figures at each end but the bulk of their large goal totals was reflected in the underlying data.

But even the xG numbers raised questions, because Chelsea benefited from 12 penalties, the joint-second-most in the past 10 Premier League seasons. Chelsea have had 14 in their 86 league games since Pochettino left. They conceded five penalties and committed the joint-most Opta-defined defensive errors leading to shots (22) in Pochettino’s season.

Across three matches in April 2024 they drew 2-2 with the bottom side Sheffield United, thumped Everton 6-0 then lost 5-0 at Arsenal. They endured a similar seesaw sequence earlier in the campaign, losing 4-1 at Tottenham and Newcastle, with a 4-4 draw against Manchester City in between. Chelsea also set the record for matches in which a team score and concede at least two goals in a 38-game Premier League season (12). How do you assess a manager’s performance in that maelstrom?

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

If the low point was not the Arsenal loss, it was being called “billion-pound bottle jobs” by Gary Neville after losing the 2024 Carabao Cup final. Never mind that Chelsea had enough chances to win, Pochettino had to answer for the defeat. Less than three months later, he was gone.

The Premier League has evolved in Pochettino’s relatively brief absence. Arne Slot arrived, won the title and left, while Guardiola’s departure leaves no big managerial beasts remaining. There have been tactical shifts, with increased man-to-man marking across the pitch, and set-piece skirmishes have decided more matches than feels healthy.

Opta’s data shows Pochettino’s probable new side move upfield more quickly but press less intensely than his Chelsea team. There will need to be an adjustment. But can a manager whose training methods at Chelsea were described by a well-placed source as “antiquated” get up to speed as quickly as United need?

Pochettino will adapt and his Premier League record commands the utmost respect. The relevance of his recent work to United in 2026-27 is less clear.

#811. Who Is Sam Hartman? What to Know About the New Bachelor Lead

The Bachelor just announced that NFL quarterback Sam Hartman will lead the ABC dating franchise’s 30th season, set to air in March 2027. See everything to know about the athlete.

The Bachelor just announced that its upcoming 30th season will have a major twist—tapping Washington Commanders quarterback Sam Hartman as the leading man for the ABC reality dating show.

“I’m excited but I’m also so nervous,” Hartman said on Good Morning America Nov. 13. “I have a tough time holding conversation with one girl. 30 is going to be pretty tough.”

Nevertheless, Hartman’s huddle couldn’t be more thrilled that he’s passing out petals instead of throwing passes.

“They’re excited,” the 27-year-old revealed of his family’s reaction to the news. “My mom and I have a really cool relationship, and my pops is obviously just supportive. And their big thing is just be myself and enjoy the experience, and you know, trust the instincts and trust your gut.”

Hartman’s casting marks the first time in years the franchise's Bachelor wasn’t picked from the pool of prior Bachelorette contestants—but that’s not the only unique quality Hartman is bringing to the Fantasy Suite.

Below, find a play-by-play of all the X’s and O’s to know about Hartman.

After playing college football at the University of Notre Dame, Hartman was drafted into the United Football League in 2024, playing for the Birmingham Stallions. That same year, he signed with the Washington Commanders as an undrafted free agent.

Hartman has remained a member of the Commanders’ practice squad and acts as their backup quarterback. He has yet to play in a regular season NFL game.

Yes, Hartman is still an active player for the Commanders, although he has not yet made his NFL debut.

After his casting in The Bachelor was announced, Hartman shared that his teammates were throwing support his way—but joked he might not catch all of it.

“My teammates were giving me some advice on the plane ride back,” he explained on Good Morning America. “So, probably not going to listen to anybody on that. But no, I'm excited.”

While Hartman will be flown around the country come hometowns, he calls Charlotte, North Carolina home.

He attended SouthLake Christian Academy in Huntersville and played three seasons of football at Davidson Day School before attending Wake Forest University prior to his transfer to Notre Dame, according to WBTV.

After being announced at the next Bachelor, Hartman admitted he’s made more than a few fumbles when it comes to his dating life. The athlete said that charming 30 women on the upcoming season, set to air in March 2027, will be “tough.”

Similarly, Hartman’s social media profiles appear to be strictly business—as most of his posts are dedicated to football.

No, Hartman is not the first football player to hand out roses. In fact, host and NFL alum Jesse Palmer—who has acted as franchise host since 2021—was a contestant himself during season five after playing in the NFL for five seasons.

Meanwhile, Golden Bachelor alum Mel Owens previously played for the Los Angeles Rams, while Colton Underwood similarly spent time with the Philadelphia Eagles, Las Vegas Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers, although he never played in a regular season NFL game.

The Bachelor season 26 star Clayton Echard also spent time with the Seattle Seahawks in 2016 for training camp.

Initially, Hartman admitted he told ABC “no way” to the proposition of becoming The Bachelor franchise’s next leading man.

“The connotation of it, I was like, ‘I don’t know,’” Hartman explained on Good Morning America. “Then, I got really lucky and talked to Jesse Palmer. He kind of gave me the insight and gave me the, what it is and what it’s not.”

Ultimately, Hartman is willing to throw a spiral into the dark if it means meeting his soulmate.

“Anybody in their right mind if you get told, ‘Hey you’ve got a chance to go find the love of your life,’” Hartman continued. “I know one thing, when people are saying ‘I do’ they don’t ask you where you met, they just ask you if you want to do it forever and I don’t see any problem with that.”

Nevertheless, the quarterback admitted he was “very nervous.”

"Did me and my ex still have a relationship prior to this?" she said. "Yes, because I didn’t think I was gonna meet anybody here."

While Kat and Dale were sent home before the final test of Paradise, their romance continued to bloom. The show revealed the alum from Zach Shallcross' season and the former contestant from Clare Crawley's went on to travel across the U.S. together and made plans to build a future together, including moving closer.

"It was tough at times," Dale commented under Kat's August 2025 Instagram post, "but we navigated it together…and I wouldn’t change a thing."

But their journey came to a close in early 2026.

Among the issues Kat detailed during a January appearance on the Bachelor Happy Hour podcast was his unwillingness to relocate from NYC.

"San Diego is apparently, to him, not anywhere he could grow his career," she explained. "I never really got full answers. I don’t really know what the true reason was."

Golden Bachelorette alum Gary Levingston and Leslie Fhima (a runner up for Golden Bachelor Gerry Turner's heart) appeared to have quite the glittery future when they were voted off Bachelor in Paradise's 10th season, even writing about "making new memories" in a post-elimination social media video. But the onetime Prince muse isn't quite sure if she wants to be his lover.

"We talk all the time," she revealed during an August 2025 appearance on Bachelor Happy Hour. "Gary is, I can honestly say right now, one of my best friends. I’ll call him if I have a problem. He kind of talks me off the ledge a little bit, and we are always there for each other. We have each other’s back."

While she acknowledged that the nearly 2,000 miles between them (she's based in Minnesota; he's in California) complicates the situation, she hasn't given up hope. "All I know is that for me, a big thing with any relationship, a romantic one for sure, is I want to be friends first," she continued. "Because I want to be with my best friend growing older."

Golden Bachelorette's head mansion man Kim Buike found someone to make sweet music with in Gerry Turner's first impression rose recipient Faith Martin. Though they were eliminated on the 10th season of Paradise, they sailed off into the sunset, with Faith posting a video to Instagram in August 2025 of the retired navy captain enjoying a hometown date with her in Washington.

However, they ultimately realized they weren't each other's person and that they were better off as friends.

"We talk sometimes two to three times a week," Faith said in a September 2025 Instagram video. "He lives five and a half hours away. But the point is this: We are not a in-love couple. Nope, we are not. We never fell in love. We had a great connection on the show."

Status: SplitGrant may have met 25 potential love interests on his first night in the Bachelor mansion, but in the end, it was Juliana Pasquarosa who scored his final rose. However, the couple decided to call it quits less than three months after their propsal aired.

“This is one of the harder things I’ve had to write, but I want to share it honestly. Juliana and I have decided to end our relationship,” Grant wrote on his Instagram Story June 13. “We both gave this our best and poured a lot of love into each other, but after a lot of deep conversations, we’ve come to the understanding that we’re simply not the right fit long term.”

Status: EngagedAfter appearing on the first-ever season of The Golden Bachelor and leaving Gerry Turner's season early, Joan Vassos handed out the roses on the debut season of The Golden Bachelorette. It was there that she met and got engaged to contestant Chock Chapple.

"We are living proof that no matter what life throws at you that there is still hope, even at our age," Joan said on The Golden Bachelorette's November 2024 finale before Chock proposed in Bora Bora. "I waited 'til this moment in this amazing location to tell you that I love you, and I want to spend the rest of my life with you. I want to wake up next to you in the morning, and I want to kiss you when I go to bed at night."

Though the pair are still navigating long-distance, they're slowly making plans for their life together.

“We have grown kids and they just happen to be falling into that part of their lives too," Joan shared in a February 2026 Instagram Q&A, explaining why they're considering a 2027 wedding date. "We'll get married sometime when our kids aren't getting married."

Status: SplitDuring the season 21 finale of The Bachelorette, it looked like The Bachelor alum Jenn Tran was finally getting her happy ending with her final pick Devin Strader. But Jenn revealed on After the Final Rose back in September 2024 that Devin gave her the cold shoulder as soon as the cameras stopped rolling.

"He was making bold proclamations of love and then suddenly the next day he was like, nothing and he denied ever being in love," Jenn told host Jesse Palmer during the Sept. 3 episode. "All the promises he had made to me, all of the love that he had wanted to give to me wasn't there anymore."

Drama continued to play out when Devin shared a 13-minute video recounting his side of the story to Instagram, where in addition to taking "accountability” he shared insight into why he ended the relationship in a 15-minute phone call.

While Jenn alleged he dumped her during the call in August, he claimed that Jenn demanded to know what was wrong as he tried to find a way to break the news in person.

"I didn't really know what else to do," he explained, noting he had been waiting to tell her in person. "She kind of forced my hand."

After that, Jenn waltzed over to Dancing With the Stars and into the heart of her partner Sasha Farber. The duo continued to dance together even after their October 2024 elimination, but split in 2025.

Status: SplitIn November 2022, Greg Grippo (one of Katie Thurston's suitors on The Bachelorette a year prior) joined Victoria Fuller on the season eight finale of Bachelor in Paradise. There, the two announced that they were in a relationship. In April 2024, he revealed the two had called it quits.

Status: SplitBefore Victoria Fuller and Greg Grippo went public with their romance on the finale of Bachelor in Paradise's eighth season, she and her costar Johnny DePhillipo ended their engagement.

Status: DivorcedGerry and Theresa Nist got engaged in November 2023 during the finale of the inaugural Golden Bachelor and tied the knot in a January 2024 televised ceremony.

However, three months after their nuptials, the couple announced that they were breaking up.

“Theresa and I have had a number of heart-to-heart conversations and we've looked closely at our situation, our living situation, so forth," Gerry said during a joint appearance on Good Morning America with Theresa April 2024. “We've come to the conclusion mutually that it's probably time for us to dissolve our marriage."

They reached a divorce settlement in June 2024, according to court records reviewed by E! News.

In April 2025, Gerry revealed on the Bachelor Happy Hour podcast that he was dating someone new and "it's going well."

Status: EngagedAfter courting 32 potential brides, tennis pro Joey found his perfect match in project manager Kelsey Anderson. "I can't wait another minute to tell you that I love you," Joey told his final rose recipient, before getting down on one knee during his season's March 2024 finale. "There is something about you. You have this infectious energy that makes me smile. It's a feeling I've never had before."Imagining his forever with the Louisiana native, he continued, "I have known for a while that I've wanted to have a beautiful life, but I truly didn't know how beautiful that life could be until I met you."

Status: SplitThough underwater welder John Henry Spurlock (one of Charity Lawson's suitors) and nurse Kat (she competed for Zach Shallcross' heart) didn't connect until midway through season nine of Bachelor in Paradise, they were willing to dive into the deep end. "We’re leading our amicable split with nothing but positivity and mutual respect for one another."

Status: SplitThough postpartum nurse Kylee Russell lamented boyfriend Aven Jones' unwillingness to get down on bended knee—a move he was purportedly prepared to make while romancing Bachelorette Rachel Recchia—she ultimately accepted Aven's Paradise proposal to "get out of here and make it work." Though that meant her planned engagement gown remained packed, "I just had to do what I felt was right," she said. "Love is all about taking risk."Two days after their December 2023 finale aired, she announced on her Instagram Stories that their relationship had "dissolved due to multiple infidelities." Aven later issued an apology to Kylee, writing, "I have made major mistakes in the relationship and hurt someone who was very close to me."

Status: Engaged"I am happy with how this season turns out!" Charity Lawson teased to E! News, a statement that way undersold her August 2023 finale. Dropping to one knee, integrative medicine specialist Dotun Olubeko proclaimed their love to be "perfect," asking the child and family therapist, "Would you do me the honor of turning this fairytale into a reality?"While their happily ever after awaits—the pair said they're considering a 2025 or 2026 wedding—the Georgia native will first take a spin through the Dancing With the Stars ballroom. "All right, baby," Dotun told Charity on The Bachelorette: After the Final Rose. Status: MarriedZach shall get his happy ending. Despite more than a few Fantasy Suite-related stumbles, Zach Shallcross ended season 27 in March 2023 down on one knee. The love I feel for you is something I could have never imagined."In July 2023, the Texas-based duo made an even bigger step in their journey, with Kaity sharing on Instagram, "Officially roommates."

They wed on May 23, 2025, in what Kaity labeled "a cute little chapel celebration." Though they'd initially planned a larger affair, "I just took a step back, and I was like, 'I don't know if we need this,'" she explained on a June 2025 episode of the Bachelor Happy Hour podcast. But one key element left her charmed. The aunt who nominated her to compete for Zach's heart found the Austin-area chapel they used for their ceremony. Said Kaity, "It was perfect."

With a heavy heart full of love for one another we have decided it is best for us to take a step back from our relationship," they said in a joint statement posted on Instagram. #810. The club preparing to play again after the death of a player

Ezekiel Williams was a "box-to-box midfielder with high energy who was not afraid of a tackle", says Hendon chairman Cyrus Cooper

"I messaged Ezekiel because we had a midweek cup game and I wanted to check he was still available," says Adam Fisher - manager of non-league Hendon.

"There was no reply. Then I found out what had happened."

Ezekiel Williams died in hospital on 2 November from head injuries after an incident in Milton Keynes. He was 26.

Known to friends as 'Zekes' and 'Eze', Williams was well known in non-league circles having played for clubs including Hastings United, Kettering Town and St Ives Town.

A midfielder, he joined Hendon in September and had already established himself at his new club as a "humble, unassuming and generous individual with razor-sharp wit".

His death has devastated the part-time club based in Kingsbury, north-west London.

"Nothing prepares you for something like this," Hendon's chairman Cyrus Cooper tells BBC Sport. "We're all human beings and the club is struggling to come to terms with what has happened."

Hendon, who play in the Isthmian League South Central Division - the eighth tier of English football, have not played since Williams died, as players and staff mourn the loss of a popular player.

On Saturday, 12 days after his death, they return to action at Bedfont Sports.

"Saturday is going to be so hard because Eze is going to be on our minds and what happened to him," Hendon midfielder Tashae Andall-Gibbons tells BBC Sport.

"Everyone is distraught. Eze was only 26 and had his whole life ahead of him."

Cooper says: "It's going to be the first time the players put their kit on without Ezekiel being there.

"I think there are going to be a lot of tears. It's going to be an emotional day for everyone associated with Hendon Football Club."

Ezekiel Williams (right) with his brother Omran and sister Shadore

Hendon's grieving players have been offered counselling as they attempt to come to terms with the loss of a team-mate who scored in a league game against Jersey Bulls as recently as 24 October.

Three days later, Williams - from Ruislip - started the 2-0 home defeat by Egham Town.

"He messaged me the day after to say: 'Gaffer, I'm really sorry I didn't catch you after the game but I'm going away for the weekend to see a relative who is sick'," says Fisher.

"He said: 'I won't be at training on Thursday, I will miss the game on Saturday but I'll be back on Monday.'

Fisher sent Williams a message on the Monday asking about his availability for a London Cup tie against Woodford, which was due to take place a couple of days later.

There was no reply. The following day, via social media, he discovered his player had died.

"I found out on the Tuesday afternoon and I didn't leave my house until the Friday," he says. "I was shocked and in a daze."

As manager of Welwyn Garden City for seven years, Fisher has delivered hundreds of team talks.

He has thought long and hard about the one he will give to his grief-stricken players on Saturday.

"What can you say that the players are going to take in?" says Fisher, who has watched interviews with Liverpool players about the impact Diogo Jota's death had on them, in an attempt to learn more about how to deal with grief inside a dressing room.

"I've got a squad of players who are mourning the loss of one of their team-mates. We are all really struggling."

Cooper adds: "Ezekiel was very courteous and softly spoken. I remember we lost a match and he came up to me after the game and apologised. That was the type of man he was."

Hendon's players say a prayer for Williams at training on Thursday

Away from Hendon, Williams coached children at football coaching company JOAP (Journey Of A Pro).

"I've had lots of messages from parents saying how much Zekes made their kids feel so special," says Tyrique Clarke - CEO and head of coaching at JOAP, and Williams' best friend.

"We met about 14 years ago and we spoke every day about everything.

"He was a real source of comfort for me. Someone I would speak to about every decision. Who do I ask now? He was just the most selfless, loving person and always a bright spark of energy."

Clarke adds: "Zekes loved coaching children. He would always give them a little Bible quote or motivational speech in team talks before games. He was just a genuine, kind-hearted person."

A crowdfunding page set up in Williams' memory has raised nearly Â£19,000.

Players and staff at Hendon have contributed, and the club will pay tribute to Williams at their next home game against Ascot United on 28 November.

Williams attended church and would send his group of friends a meaningful Bible verse every day

Williams' sister Shadore paid tribute to her brother.

"Seeing Ezekiel get older and gain different ambitions in life was the best thing I could have witnessed," she said., external

"He got to become a football coach and teach children who loved the same sport as he did.

"He became closer to God and said he wanted to attend church and would get excited each time he got a new suit and would show it off to the family."

On Thursday, Hendon's players met up for training to try to prepare for Saturday's game.

The chairman attended to give a speech after a traumatic week for the club, while Hendon's players said a prayer for their team-mate.

"Everybody is still trying to process what has happened," adds Andall-Gibbons. "I hope we use this pain in the right way and put on a big performance on Saturday.

#809. ‘No one is unbeatable’: Tuchel eager for England to impose style on Spain

Manager calls Sunday’s Nations League decider a ‘final’ as preparations for Euro 2028 ratchet up a level

Proof of concept. It is Thomas Tuchel’s latest buzz phrase. The England manager has dropped it into the conversation pretty regularly since the Friday of last week when he named his squad for this international window, the one that was always going to decide whether his team finished first or second in their Nations League group.

By it, Tuchel means a test of his methods, what he is trying to build – or, more accurately, fine-tune – as he turns his gaze towards Euro 2028 and tries to move on from the devastation of the World Cup semi-final exit against Argentina. The test does not come any bigger than the one which faces him and his players in Madrid on Sunday night.

England ticked off part one of the mission at Wembley on Thursday when they defeated Croatia 2-1. Now for the serious business: Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium. The win over Croatia ensured that England retained a puncher’s chance of top spot, which would in theory bring easier opposition in the two-leg quarter-finals in March. Victory over the world and European champions – nothing less – would secure it owing to England’s superior goal difference.

Tuchel is calling it a “final” and he wants this. “Yeah, push our limits, see where we are,” he said. Remember England’s previous Nations League campaign when they were in the second tier? The team learned little from the ties against the Republic of Ireland, Finland and Greece – except that it was unwise of Lee Carsley, the interim manager, to jam in all of the glamour No 10s against Greece at Wembley. The matches did not help England in their preparations for the World Cup.

This is different because Spain are the country to beat. They have lost only once in 43 games and that was on penalties to Portugal in the 2025 Nations League final. Technically, it went down as a draw (even if nobody thinks it was) and so Spain’s run, which began in March 2024, is considered (by some) the longest unbeaten in men’s international history. Since they drew 0-0 with Cape Verde in their opening World Cup group game, they have won 12 straight, including all five of their Nations League matches.

Tuchel, his staff, the players and the Football Association regard the Nations League as a springboard into the Euros when England will co-host. They are desperate to reach the four-team finals tournament next June because it would ensure continued high-grade opposition. And they are desperate to lift the trophy, mainly because winning is a good habit. It is easy to feel that England’s fans are not as invested. Expect that to change if the team advance to the finals, especially if those games were in England, which would be a possibility.

Tuchel has re-geared his personnel this season, partly because of injuries but not entirely. He had only 11 players from the World Cup in his squad against Croatia; two more – Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence – hope to return against Spain after injury niggles. The manager is using different players, most notably Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ben White, Lewis Hall, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Alex Scott and Rio Ngumoha. Lewis-Skelly is back from a one-game ban against Spain. Scott is out injured; it felt significant that he was at Wembley to watch the Croatia game. Tuchel wants to keep him close.

Tuchel’s main tactical tweak has been to give Jude Bellingham greater licence to drift from the No 10 role, to overload on either side, to run on intuition. But it is not only Bellingham. Others have been encouraged to push into out-of-the-ordinary zones, including the full-backs. It is no longer a positional team approach. The idea is that it is freer, more fluid. Tuchel is obsessed with finding ways to accelerate the play through midfield.

The principles remain. Aggression, physicality, working hard on the cover. Intensity, including when pressing high. Are England the most economical team? No. Tuchel is aware of this. He just wants to go for it and see whether his England can impose their style on Spain. It was the same when they played them at Wembley in the Nations League opener and there were good periods before Spain ran out 3-2 winners. This time, Tuchel wants more.

“It’s not a must-win game if you go to Spain,” he said. “But the mindset is important. Beating Croatia so we could have this match was the first step and now it’s important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home [against Spain] – attack them, try to make it a physical game, impose our strength. And we will. I’m very confident about that.”

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Tuchel felt England deserved more from the topsy-turvy match against Spain at Wembley when his team conceded early and were almost overwhelmed in the first 35 minutes. They stabilised and went 2-1 up before the game turned when Harry Kane missed a penalty for 3-1.

“Once we got our energy going and played with this for the equaliser for 1-1, we were strong,” Tuchel said. “Harry’s penalty was maybe the key moment for us because we were very strong then and deserved to be 3-1 up. It would have been very difficult for Spain to come back against us. We had too many big individual mistakes in our own half on the night.

“But honestly, if you deeply look into the [Nations League] matches … Spain had some crucial ball losses against Croatia [in Split] and got away with it. They conceded some big, big chances and still managed to win in the end [with an 88th-minute Mikel Merino winner]. So no one is unbeatable. We’re full of confidence. It’s exactly what we wanted. We feel that we have something to take that we lost the last time.”

Tuchel was tetchy at the beginning of the first Nations League window in September, the wounds still raw from the criticism after the Argentina defeat. Everyone was on egg shells. The mood has greatly improved and Tuchel is back to his old self; eyes twinkling, in control. He was asked whether England had come a long way since the summer.

“Yeah, I think we’re there,” Tuchel said. “We’re ready to win on Sunday. I know what it takes and while no one can ever guarantee it, I think it’s the moment to check how far we are. And proof of concept.”

#808. Deck the Halls for Less With Festive Christmas Decor Under $50

Getting your home decorated for the holiday season doesn't have to cost a lot! We found garlands, lights, trees & more under $50.

We're here to prove that decking the halls doesn't have to be so expensive! We scoured some of our favorite spots to shop for home decor, and rounded up plenty of festive fun for under $50.

This Vampire Survivors spin-off has a lot of love for the famous grimdark sci-fi universe, but without the intimidatingly dense lore and complex systems.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

We've had no shortage of great Warhammer 40K games lately, but most aren't exactly aimed at the casual crowd. Warhammer Survivors changes that, finally providing curious gamers with an easy entry point into the grim darkness of the 41st millennium.

Developed by Auroch Digital (in collaboration with Vampire Survivors' Poncle), this new spin on the survivors-like roguelite subgenre mixes the sci-fi 40,000 setting with the pure fantasy Age of Sigmar universe. This means heroes and enemies from all over the Warhammer mythos meet together in a bite-sized game that anyone can figure out and enjoy in less than five minutes.

When you look at the alternatives, that's a remarkable achievement for a franchise that's notoriously hard (and often expensive) to get into.

Warhammer Survivors isn't bogged down by dense lore, involved mechanics, or massive campaign playthroughs. It's more of an "inspired by" effort that gives casuals a small taste of the series' iconic characters — including Boltgun's Malum Caedo — and factions like the terrifying Tyranids, the raucous Orks, and the foul forces of Chaos.

All of 40K's (and Age of Sigmar's) recognizable elements are on display, but they serve more as flavoring sprinkled on top of Vampire Survivors' successful formula.

If you're new to the Survivors-like subgenre, it's a unique gaming experience. You battle an endless onslaught of enemies that slowly march towards you, with your character passively attacking automatically. You only need to move them around sprawling arenas and select level-up upgrades and items after collecting enough gems (skulls in this case).

The moment-to-moment gameplay is as simple as it can get outside of walking sims and interactive "experiences," but there's a deceiving depth to item synergies and how to correctly "build" characters to endure all the carnage.

Unlike Poncle's original game, Warhammer Survivors struggles a bit to get going. The early hours are sluggish until you unlock certain meta upgrades, but its still got that Vampire Survivors magic at its core.

As far as "podcast/gym games" go, this is a perfect fit. There's just enough going on to keep one's brain engaged, but minimal inputs and a tight overarching design lead to a rhythm that's easy to get into without using much brainpower. It's oddly satisfying to weave through enemies and level up your firepower, watching a single Astra Militarum grunt grow into a full Lasgun-spamming, chainsword-wielding wrecking ball.

Achievement and unlock hunters will find enough to bite into here, too. It's unclear if the devs will continue to add more Warhammer 40K and Age of Sigmar deep cuts to this game via DLCs and free updates, but those universes have daunting depths to explore. This really could become a gateway game for future 40K fans: by the time they realize they're hooked, they'll already have 2000 pts of space marines painted and ready to play.

As massive sci-fi and fantasy properties try to aggressively expand and absorb more and more fans, it's easy to pander to already-converted diehards too much. And sure, we can't wait for strategy heavyweights like Dawn of War 4 and Total War: WH40K either, but they're hardly good recommendations for folks who don't even know what a Space Marine is or why the robotic Necrons are so grumpy.

Warhammer Survivors won't answer those questions beyond the surface-level iconography, but it's fun enough to push those curious to dig deeper and embrace the same material in more mature video game genres... and maybe even pick up a few miniatures.

Warhammer Survivors is now available on PC (Steam & GOG), PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 1/2, and mobile (iOS & Android). It's also playable on Game Pass.

#806. Liverpool and Van Dijk have a decision to make

Virgil van Dijk joined Liverpool for Â£75m from Southampton in January 2018

After Liverpool beat Brighton in October, Virgil van Dijk went upstairs to one of the hospitality lounges at Anfield and met up with Alan Hansen.

It was Van Dijk who, at the end of the 2024-25 season, asked the former Liverpool and Scotland defender to present him with the Premier League trophy and this time they posed for a picture that inevitably did the rounds on social media.

Whenever the time comes for Van Dijk to move on from Liverpool, he will go down as arguably their greatest centre-half, alongside Hansen. The question now is whether he will finish his career at Anfield like Hansen did in 1991.

Van Dijk's contract expires next summer and, even if the 35-year-old insisted this week that he was in no panic, it is a topic that will be a source of debate until a decision is made.

"Let's see what the season brings. I've had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that's the case. If not, then I will go somewhere else," the Liverpool captain told reporters at Selhurst Park.

Two seasons ago, with Van Dijk in a similar situation, there was a similar sense of calm and come April 2025 he signed a two-year-deal.

Judging by Van Dijk's comments there is a feeling of him wanting to stay, but both he and Liverpool have an important decision to make.

Van Dijk and Alan Hansen are regarded as two of Liverpool's greatest defenders

Aside from a poor error against Villarreal in the Champions League, Van Dijk has shown this season that his standards haven't dropped.

His partnership with Jeremy Jacquet, who joined in the summer, is going from strength to strength and Van Dijk has played every minute in the Premier League since the start of last season.

A "little niggle" has affected him in recent weeks and this is the first international window he has missed with the Netherlands since Euro 2020, but it isn't a major cause for concern.

Liverpool have lost a number of senior figures in recent years but Van Dijk remains a leader in every form, and that was evidenced by his suggestion to Andoni Iraola that the squad should visit the museum at Anfield to learn more about the club's history.

At Crystal Palace on Sunday, it spoke volumes of Van Dijk's character that he came over to a group of reporters and asked if they wanted to speak to him, rather than the other way around. He regularly fronts up, regardless of the result.

Van Dijk is certainly not the force he was under Jurgen Klopp but he remains an elite centre-half and the stats justify that.

Per 90 minutes this season in the Premier League, he averages 60.7 successful passes per game, wins possession 3.5 times and makes 7.1 clearances. He has a 75% success in duels and 79% when it comes to aerial duels.

In his first full season at the club, in 2018-19, he averaged 72.4 successful passes per game, won possession 5.1 times and made 5.3 clearances. He had a 76% success in duels and 75% when it came to aerial duels.

That said, the Liverpool hierarchy will have seen the way the situation with Mohamed Salah unfolded last year and will be keen to avoid a repeat. After a stellar season in 2024-25, Salah's numbers plummeted in 2025-26.

Liverpool have a number of young centre-backs within their ranks, from Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni to the likes of Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Mor Talla Ndiaye, but letting Van Dijk go would be a risk and leave a gaping hole.

He didn't take a pay cut in 2025 and continues to earn a salary understood to be in the region of Â£400,000 a week.

Joe Gomez, 29, is also out of contract this summer and Liverpool do have an option to buy Ronald Araujo, 27, at the end of the season from Barcelona but there would be a clear loss of experience and leadership if Van Dijk leaves.

For sporting director Julian Ward, the future of the Dutchman will be a priority over the coming months.

Providing he is fit, Van Dijk will make his 390th appearance for Liverpool when they take on Manchester United after the international break.

And given his consistency, he is likely to reach 400 appearances by the end of the year. He would become only the 28th Liverpool player to do so.

The 31 goals he has scored for Liverpool in the Premier League is the most for a defender at the club.

In terms of a resolution with his contract, this is likely to be one where both parties bide their time and, given that the existing relationships are strong and there's a mutual respect, it would not be a surprise to see negotiations go into 2027.

Come January, Van Dijk will be able to sign a pre-contract agreement with an overseas club and as such, AC Milan and Juventus are monitoring the situation.

Sources in Turkey are also hopeful that they could tempt him to make the same move as Salah if an extension isn't agreed at Liverpool but, as it stands, it would be quite a surprise if Van Dijk moved on this summer.

#805. Football Daily | Taking a brief minute to remember Pierre Sage’s impact at Crystal Palace

Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!

So farewell then, Pierre Sage. Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate. The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug.

His supporters, such as they are, would argue he was hobbled by knack, suspensions and poor transfer dealings, and approximately nothing went to plan for the man who just six months ago was revelling in being named Ligue 1 coach of the year. His philosophy just never quite translated. “There are two types of teams: one with the ball, and the other chasing it,” he said last year. “I prefer to be the first of those.” And it is true that in Ligue 1 last season only Paris St-Germain and Marseille had, on average, more of the ball than his Lens side. But it turned out that Crystal Palace players were quite happy chasing it thank you, whichever of them he picked – and he picked most of them, fielding more players than any other club this season.

They are averaging 43.2% possession, more than only Coventry and Hull. Against Tottenham at the end of October – when, to be fair, they were hobbled by a 13th-minute red card – they had the ball just 20.8% of the time – which, at least since 2013-14, they’ve never come close to equalling – and ended with an xG of 0.14 – not as bad as the 0.12 they registered against Manchester City in August 2022 (a game which, somehow, they ended with two goals), but worse than all their other ones. “It is,” Sage sighed after the Spurs match, “a disaster.” In that interview Sage said his “main principles” included “to look to get behind the opposition defence non-stop; and to press your opponents hard so you can win the ball back quickly,” Again, lovely ideas.

But Sage’s Palace were absolutely rubbish at pressing – on Opta’s pressed sequences metric, measuring “the number of open-play sequences starting in their defensive third where the opposition has three or fewer passes and the sequence ends in their own half”, they are currently bottom of the league, and what high turnovers they have managed have led to just eight shots (second-bottom) and no goals (bottom). As for getting behind the opposition defence non-stop, Opta has recorded 24 through-balls this season, which actually is the fifth-highest total in the league. They have also recorded 23 offsides. Still, we should take a minute (but no more) to mark another coach’s departure. Farewell, Pierre, and good luck. You certainly had none of it over here.

#804. 'It's a shootout' - Wales out to derail stuttering Norway

Former Wales captain Craig Bellamy took over as head coach in July 2024

As the first snow of the season falls in Oslo, the clean-up operation at Norway's home stadium is in full swing â tractors on the pitch, Norwegian Football Federation staff getting stuck in with their shovels.

This has been a problematic pitch in the past, with even the great Erling Haaland questioning its condition, external back in March, before it was fixed during the summer.

By their recent, historic high standards, Norway need something of a repair job themselves.

Having gone through 2025 unbeaten and then soared to the quarter-finals of the World Cup, Norway have lost three games in a row for the first time in a decade.

Granted, two of those were against Portugal, whereas their losing run in 2016 included defeats in Azerbaijan and Belarus.

But this is Norway's golden generation. With Haaland, Martin Odegaard and a glut of other elite talents at their disposal, expectations are greater than ever.

Thumping Italy twice on their way to World Cup qualification was one thing â their first major tournament since 1998 â but beating Brazil in their last-16 tie in New Jersey underlined their credentials as an emerging force in international football.

So, when this Nations League campaign came around, Stale Solbakken's men were expected to be jostling with Portugal for top spot.

Instead, they find themselves at the bottom of Group A4 with just one win from four games, level with third-placed Wales on three points but below them because of their head-to-head record.

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live Sports Extra, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

How do you stop Haaland? Wales show how it's done

Odegaard backing Norway to avenge Wales defeat

Wales' only victory of the campaign so far was against Norway in Cardiff a month ago, and on Saturday they are bidding to join Portugal and world champions Spain as the only teams to win competitive matches in Oslo over the past three years.

"The way we look at it is this is the type of game we want to be playing in," Wales head coach Craig Bellamy tells BBC Sport Wales.

"I see a collective team that you have to like but, individually, very much so as well. So that's a good challenge.

"We've all been aware of their threat. The World Cup proved that. And I just don't see them going anywhere for the next five, 10 years either."

There is much on the line for Wales and Norway in Oslo.

While either team could still reach the Nations League quarter-finals, the priority is to avoid relegation from the top tier.

Finishing third or higher would also guarantee top seeding for Euro 2028 qualifying, enabling them to avoid being drawn alongside the continent's heavyweights.

"It'll go a long way to us having an opportunity of being seeded one, which is huge for us, but it isn't going to be given to us," Bellamy adds.

"We have to go out there tomorrow and try and take it. So, for me, it's fight fire with fire. I'm expecting them to really come with big intensity and it's up to us to match it.

Staff clear snow off the pitch at Ullevaal Stadion in Oslo on Friday

If Norway are at the peak of their golden era, Wales are still basking in the afterglow of theirs.

They had been absent from major tournaments for 58 years before a team featuring Gareth Bale and Aaron Ramsey took them to the semi-finals of Euro 2016.

Like Norway's exploits this summer, that tournament in France changed the landscape of Welsh football, paving the way for future qualifications at Euro 2020 and the 2022 World Cup.

"I think that we are both small countries, so I can agree on that," Norway head coach Solbakken says of the comparison.

"Everyone will remember that summer of 2026 in Norway, as Wales did 10 years ago."

If you want to stretch the analogy to tenuous lengths, you could also note that the two teams were built around the heroics of hitherto ponytailed forwards (Bale and Haaland) and the creativity of Arsenal playmakers (Ramsey and Odegaard).

Few remain of that Welsh vintage by now, though captain Ben Davies is one.

"They've got players now performing at the highest level in world football and starring in that as well," the Tottenham Hotspur defender says.

"Great for Norwegian football, a challenge for us, but one we're looking forward to."

Davies played an important role in Wales' win over Norway last month, at the heart of a defence which managed to contain Haaland.

The 33-year-old has also been part of a Spurs backline which denied the Norwegian a goal in a 4-0 win at Manchester City two years ago.

Not that Davies is going to mention that in Oslo.

"He's a world-class player," he says. "Maybe he had an off-night [in Cardiff] but we worked hard, stuck to our job and we defended really well. Hopefully we'll do that again."

#802. Catherine Zeta-Jones’ Daughter Carys Wears Mom’s Gucci Top to Event

Catherine Zeta-Jones’ daughter Carys Douglas, 23, wore a vintage Gucci top her mom first wore back in 1996.

Carys Douglas has no reservations about borrowing from her mom’s closet.

In fact, when the 23-year-old stepped out to the Gucci x Moda Operandi event in New York City on November 11, she did so in a vintage top from the designer brand her mom Catherine Zeta-Jones wore back in the ‘90s.

The black lace top in question features a snap at the chest and features long sleeves. Carys styled the semi-sheer garment with a lacy black miniskirt, tights and a Gucci purse.

Back in 1996, however, Catherine—who shares Carys with husband Michael Douglas in addition 26-year-old son Dylan Michael Douglas—opted for a set, pairing the top with matching lacy leggings, a black bag and black heels. At the time, she donned the ensemble for the Los Angeles premiere of the film The Long Kiss Goodnight, which starred Geena Davis and Samuel L. Jackson.

As for Carys, she’s previously admitted she doesn’t mind donning the mask of Catherine when it comes to fashion.

“I love vintage clothes,” she told People in October 2025. “I’m not really into fast fashion stuff, just for sustainability reasons, so I feel very lucky that I have a wonderful closet that I can pick from.”

As for whether her mom was privy to her closet raids, Carys admitted, “I should probably tell her more, because I snag a little too much. She’s like, ‘Is that my bag?’ I’m like, ‘I don’t know. I don’t think so.’”

As for where her own career takes her, the Brown University graduate noted, “I grew up doing theater, and I didn’t study acting in school, but that’s why I’m happy to be in such an informative arts space, so hopefully more of that.”

Which is why she was more than ready to accompany her dad to the Nov. 4 Art of Freedom Gala 2026 in New York City, where he was honored with the Lifetime Achievement Award by the Tibet House US for his decades of peace advocacy.

Carys’ brother Dylan joined the father-daughter pair for the evening, making the event a truly special family affair for Michael, who is also dad to son Cameron, 47, with ex-wife Diandra Luker.

"A wonderful night in NYC with @carys.douglas and @dylan__douglas," the Basic Instinct star wrote on Instagram at the time. "Thank you to @tibethouse.us for honoring me with the Art of Freedom Award. Truly grateful for this special recognition and for such a memorable evening!"

As for more stars who share special bonds with their kids, read on.

Teyana Taylor, Junie Shumpert & Rue Shumpert

Looking more like sisters, there's one resemblance after another between the Oscar nominee and her daughters, who she shares with NBA alum Iman Shumpert.

The "Beautiful Soul" singer and wife Katie Peterson's little boy is the spitting image of his father.

Jodie Sweetin, Zoie Herpin & Beatrix Sweetin Coyle

Full House alum's, uh, full house includes her lookalike eldest daughter Zoie (left) and her two years younger little sis Beatrix.
